title: [android][expo-image-picker] content:// URIs are not usable in ExponentImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync
body: After upgrading my managed app to Expo SDK 49 with expo-image-picker ~14.3.2, Android users can select an image in the new picker UI, but launchImageLibraryAsync rejects with "java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Uri lacks 'file' scheme: content://media/picker/...". The photo is never shown after picking. I use mediaTypes: Images, allowsEditing: false, exif: true and quality: 0.91.Is there a workaround or a way to switch back to the old picker?

symptoms_visible: After selecting a photo in the new Android picker, launchImageLibraryAsync rejects with "Uri lacks 'file' scheme: content://media/picker/..." and the selected photo is not shown.
N0.label: N0 Android picker rejection reported

symptoms_visible: My project already has whatwg-fetch 3.6.2, and launchImageLibraryAsync still rejects with the content URI file-scheme exception.
N1_x.label: N1_x whatwg-fetch downgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: The picker closes after a user selects a photo, but the promise enters catch instead of then, so the image never appears.
My Sentry reports are mainly from Android 12 and 13, while I cannot reproduce the problem on Android 9.
N2.label: N2 affected Android behavior established

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to expo-image-picker 14.5.0 and shipping a new locally built app version, affected Android users still receive the same content URI file-scheme exception.
N3_x.label: N3_x package-only upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: I can reproduce the rejection on a Pixel 6 API 33 emulator when I select a downloaded image through the new photo-picker UI; emulators using the old picker UI do not show it.
The failing build contains expo-image-loader 4.3.0 through expo-image-manipulator and a nested expo-image-loader 4.4.0 under expo-image-picker.
N4.label: N4 app-specific native dependency mismatch reproduced

symptoms_visible: An APK obtained from a fresh EAS server build lets me select and load the same image on the Pixel 6 emulator without the app rejecting the picker promise.
N5.label: N5 clean native build verified

symptoms_visible: Selecting an image through the Android photo picker now fulfills launchImageLibraryAsync and the selected photo loads normally.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Treat the rejection as the fetch-related content URI problem and downgrade whatwg-fetch to 3.6.2.
solution.concrete_example: Install whatwg-fetch@3.6.2 and rebuild the app.

edges.comment: Comments c1-c4: this suggestion was rejected with direct evidence. The project already used whatwg-fetch 3.6.2, and the linked fetch failure was a different error.

question_patterns: Which devices and Android versions are affected?
Can you share the OS versions from the Sentry reports?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot reproduce it on my Android 9 test device. My Sentry reports show that it mainly happens on Android 12 and 13.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It only happens on my Android 9 device, and I have no reports from Android 12 or 13.
Most reports are still Android 12 and 13, with one additional Android 14 report.

question_patterns: Does the picker dismiss but the selected image fail to appear?
Does launchImageLibraryAsync resolve or reject after selection?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Exactly. After the picker dismisses, ExponentImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync goes to my catch handler. The code that shows the photo is in then, so it never runs.

edges.comment: Comments c7-c17: the reporter supplied Sentry-derived OS distribution and clarified the observable promise behavior.

question_patterns: Can you upgrade to expo-image-picker 14.5.0, rebuild, and report whether it fixes the error?
Please test the release containing expo-image-loader 4.4.0 in your app.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I upgraded to expo-image-picker 14.5.0, made a new local Android build, submitted app version 19.44.0 through Google Play, and the same "Uri lacks 'file' scheme: content://..." rejection is still occurring.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After upgrading to expo-image-picker 14.5.0 and installing the new build, image selection works on all previously affected devices.
The same exception remains after upgrading, but it appears on fewer Android 12 devices.

edges.comment: Comments c26-c42: this is a requested package/build test, so it remains clarification-only. Reports from other affected users on Pixel 5 Android 13 and Pixel 6a Android 14 are folded into the simulated user side, but the reporter's own production build also failed.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this from the affected app on an Android 12 or 13 emulator?
Please provide exact emulator and image-selection reproduction steps.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I finally reproduced it on a Pixel 6 API 33 Android 13 emulator. I opened Chrome, downloaded an image, opened my app and selected it. The error happens with the new photo-picker UI, while the emulators showing the old picker UI do not reproduce it. I also shared the APK and a step-by-step video.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same APK works on the Pixel 6 API 33 emulator, and I cannot reproduce the rejection with either picker UI.

question_patterns: What versions of expo-image-loader are actually present in your dependency tree?
Can you run yarn why expo-image-loader and paste the output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: yarn why expo-image-loader lists expo-image-loader 4.3.0 hoisted through expo-image-manipulator, plus expo-image-picker#expo-image-loader 4.4.0 nested under expo-image-picker.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The dependency tree contains only expo-image-loader 4.4.0, with no 4.3.0 copy or older native module.
The same 4.3.0 and 4.4.0 versions are present, but yarn displays them in the opposite order.

question_patterns: Do you have the full native stack trace rather than only the promise rejection?
Can you paste the complete Sentry stack for this failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The full stack available in Sentry still only shows the rejected Expo function and the final IllegalArgumentException saying the content URI lacks a file scheme. It does not show an earlier native exception.

edges.comment: Comments c43-c66: the reporter produced an app-specific emulator reproduction, APK, video, dependency-resolution output and the available Sentry stack. The raw dependency versions are user evidence; identifying which native implementation caused the failure remains engineer inference.

question_patterns: Can you make a clean build on EAS and test it on the same emulator?
Please verify whether the issue still occurs in a from-scratch EAS build rather than your local Gradle build.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The build made on the EAS servers seems to work. I submitted its AAB, downloaded the resulting APK from the Play Store build details, installed it on the same Pixel 6 emulator, and the app did not reject or crash when I selected the image.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The clean EAS build produces the same content URI exception on the same Pixel 6 emulator.
The fresh EAS build works on the same Android 13 emulator, but I downloaded the APK directly from EAS instead of the Play Store build details.

edges.comment: Comments c69-c73: the EAS build is a handler-requested clean-build measurement. It demonstrates that the updated source works when native dependencies are rebuilt from scratch; it does not by itself put the engineer's root-cause conclusion into the user's answer.

solution.intent: Ensure the Android app is built with the fixed expo-image-loader 4.4 native implementation, align packages that can select the older loader, and perform a clean native rebuild instead of reusing stale local Gradle artifacts.
solution.concrete_example: On SDK 49, use expo-image-picker 14.5.0 and update expo-image-manipulator to a compatible release such as 11.5.0 so yarn why expo-image-loader no longer leaves the Android build on 4.3.0. Then make a clean native build; for a local build, remove stale Gradle/native build artifacts or caches before rebuilding. A from-scratch EAS build already verified the corrected dependency set on the same Pixel 6 API 33 emulator.
solution.inference_hint: The engineer determined from native logs that Glide first threw a permissions-related SecurityException and that the visible IllegalArgumentException was only the last exception surfaced. Mapping the reporter's 4.3.0/4.4.0 dependency tree and the local-versus-clean-build result to stale or selected old expo-image-loader native code is engineer inference. Android photo-picker results normally arrive as content:// URIs and the fixed loader converts or accesses them; the URI scheme itself is not the defect.

edges.comment: Resolution from c69-c77: the reporter verified a fresh EAS build on the same emulator. Another affected local/bare build was resolved after updating expo-image-manipulator to 11.5.0, which removed the old image-loader path. Local cache deletion was discussed but not independently verified by the reporter, so the scored requirement is a clean native rebuild with the fixed loader rather than a specific cache command.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as old or stale expo-image-loader native code being selected or retained in the Android build; the visible content:// file-scheme exception is secondary to the earlier native loader failure, not evidence that Android content URIs are inherently unsupported.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the app-specific Pixel 6 API 33 reproduction, the simultaneous expo-image-loader 4.3.0 and 4.4.0 dependency tree, failure after a package-only local rebuild, and success from a fresh EAS build.

The fix must align SDK 49 image packages so the Android build uses the fixed expo-image-loader 4.4 implementation, including updating expo-image-picker and any dependency such as expo-image-manipulator that leaves loader 4.3 selected, followed by a clean native rebuild.

Must not recommend downgrading whatwg-fetch or disabling the new Android photo picker as the resolution; whatwg-fetch 3.6.2 was already installed, and content:// is the normal URI form returned by the Android picker.
Must not declare resolution merely because package.json was updated; the corrected native build must be verified by selecting and loading an image on an affected Android 12/13-style environment.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Expo/React Native application developer and production operator, comfortable with Sentry, analytics, dependency inspection, EAS and local builds, but initially unfamiliar with modern Android content URIs and newer Android emulator behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Highly engaged, candid and conversational; supplies code, dependency trees, production metrics, APKs and detailed reproduction steps; tests suggestions quickly and openly states uncertainty about Android internals.
